title: Verifier–Agent Co-Design to Reduce Verifier Tax in Agentic NetOps Planning (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does runtime verifier feedback integrated into LLM planning (co-design) reduce verifier-induced blocking of safe plans and increase safe end-to-end completion rate relative to a static post-hoc verifier, without materially increasing planning latency, across multiple NetOps task classes (routing, ACL, VLAN) in a deterministic emulated testbed?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The co-design condition (runtime verifier feedback) yields a higher safe end-to-end completion rate than the static post-hoc verifier condition (paired difference > 0).
H2: Co-design does not increase median planning latency by more than 20% relative to static verification (non-inferiority margin: 20%).
exploratory_questions: E1: How do verifier interventions (counts, types) differ by task class (routing, ACL, VLAN)?
E2: How sensitive are outcomes to verifier-feedback intensity (three deterministic levels)?
E3: What failure-mode distributions (syntax, semantic-mismatch, unsafe execution) differ between conditions?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task corpus (three task classes: routing, ACL, VLAN)
Deterministic emulated execution using containerized network simulator images (two topology classes: small spine-leaf and medium enterprise) described below
Evaluation strictly bounded to the supplied synthetic/emulated testbed and published task generator
model_scope: Hosted LLM API: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (api.openai.com) — version as-of-execution logged; temperature=0.0; max_tokens=1024; deterministic decoding prompts and fixed seeds for any stochastic subroutines
Single base LLM used for both conditions to avoid model-family confounds
transformation_scope: NL→DSL translation prompt templates and post-generation deterministic parser to canonical DSL
Verifier feedback primitives (constraint assertions, counterexample traces, prune signals) encoded as JSON messages exchanged with planner
Execution trace extraction (emulator stdout/stderr and deterministic verdicts) for safety labelling
secondary_estimands: distributional differences in failure-mode proportions by task class
sampling_plan: Paired design. Each unique task instance is executed twice (once under Static post-hoc verifier (baseline) and once under Co-design runtime verifier feedback (guarded)), forming one paired observation. Task corpus: 2 topology classes × per-topology task instances = total tasks per scenario (see budget scenarios). Inclusion: tasks produced by the published task-generator script using provided seeds. Exclusion: tasks whose emulator setup fails deterministically (see retry policy). Randomization: task ordering randomized with fixed seed 42 for execution order only; pairing preserved. Retry policy: up to 2 automated infra-retries for transient emulator or API failures; if a retry succeeds both runs of the pair are kept; if retries exhaust and one condition completed while the other failed, pair is marked incomplete and excluded from the primary analysis (complete-pair primary). Sensitivity: secondary analysis treats incomplete pairs as failed (success=0) for guarded and baseline as described in analysis plan.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses the supplied 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' contract (executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1) computing the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary dataset: all complete pairs (both conditions produced final execution outcome within retry policy). Primary test: two-sided paired test (contract will use exact paired test or its internal preferred method); report mean paired difference with 95% CI. Failed-call treatment for primary: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' — incomplete pairs counted as failures for robustness. Secondary analyses: paired median latency ratio (report Cohen's d or nonparametric effect size), verifier-block-rate difference, and stratified analyses by task class. Multiple comparisons: single primary confirmatory estimand; Holm-Bonferroni correction applied across secondary estimands and exploratory contrasts. All analysis code deterministic, seeds logged, result schema: paired_binary_episode_v1.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference). All other outcomes (latency, block rate, failure-mode proportions, feedback-intensity ablations, task-class strata) are secondary or exploratory. Apply Holm-Bonferroni correction across the set of secondary hypotheses; exploratory analyses reported without confirmatory p-value thresholds and marked exploratory.
missingness_plan: Primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary). Automated retry policy as specified in sampling_plan. Sensitivity analysis reinterprets any incomplete pair as a failed success (0) in both conditions for conservative bounds. All exclusions and number of incomplete pairs reported with reasons (infra-failure, API quota, deterministic emulator error). No human adjudication is permitted; all treatments are deterministic and logged.

benchmark_names: Synthetic NetOps intent→configuration corpus v1 (published generator and seeds)
Containerized emulator topology images (small spine-leaf, medium enterprise) v1
risk_factors: Task-corpus leakage between development and final run (pre-lock artifacts)
Public-model pretraining exposure to synthetic corpus (unknown)
detection_procedures: Deterministic artifact hashing (SHA256) of every generated task instance and emulator configuration; compare to pre-lock corpus hashes to detect pre-lock leakage.
Provenance log of generator seed and parameters for each task; detect duplicates by exact-match hashing.
Automated check for identical NL prompts and DSL outputs across pairs; flag exact duplicates.
item_flagging_rules: If task hash appears in pre-lock development artifact list → flag contaminated and exclude from primary analysis.
If task duplicates another task within the same scenario (identical seed/parameters) → collapse into single instance and remove duplicates deterministically.
If emulator configuration hash mismatches declared topology image hash → exclude task run and mark as infra-failure.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Contaminated items are excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis; report excluded-item counts and conduct sensitivity analysis including contaminated items and/or reweighted analyses. All contamination detections and exclusions are deterministic and logged; no human adjudication is used.
residual_uncertainty: Residual uncertainty remains about model pretraining exposure to similar public artifacts (cannot be eliminated); sensitivity analyses reported.
Emulator ecological validity vs. production networks remains a noncritical external-validity limitation (reported separately).

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative low-budget pilot: 100 paired tasks (50 per topology). Intended as quick-check replication and method debug. Recommended for debugging only; underpowered for small effects.
models: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (hosted) — same base LLM for both conditions
transformations: NL→DSL prompt generation and deterministic parsing; verifier JSON feedback messages (3-level feedback intensity pre-registered)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task average LLM calls estimate = 6 (3 calls per condition × 2 conditions). 100 tasks × 6 calls/task = 600 model calls. Two topology classes: 50 tasks each.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended balanced scenario powered for the primary estimand: 200 paired tasks (100 per topology).
models: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (hosted) — same base LLM for both conditions
transformations: NL→DSL prompt generation and deterministic parsing; verifier JSON feedback messages (three deterministic intensity levels)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task average LLM calls estimate = 6 (3 calls per condition × 2 conditions). 200 tasks × 6 calls/task = 1,200 model calls, within capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10,000). Two topology classes: 100 tasks each. This scenario is recommended because power calculations (see power_plan) indicate ~80% power to detect an absolute paired difference ≈10 percentage points under the stated assumptions.

budget_scenarios.description: High-powered scenario for detecting smaller effects and richer stratified analysis: 400 paired tasks (200 per topology).
models: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (hosted) — same base LLM for both conditions
transformations: Full logged NL→DSL pipelines and verifier feedback traces
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task average LLM calls estimate = 6. 400 tasks × 6 = 2,400 model calls. Feasible under manifest limits but requires proportionally more wall-clock time and cost.

power_plan.clustering_unit: task (paired within-task comparison: guarded vs baseline)
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal-approximation paired-proportion power calculation with conservative variance estimate and assumed within-task outcome correlation ρ = 0.5. Power target 80%, two-sided α=0.05.
assumptions: Baseline safe completion rate (static verifier) assumed 0.60 for planning; guarded condition expected to be higher under H1.
Within-task correlation between outcomes (guarded vs baseline) assumed ρ = 0.5; sensitivity analyses sweep ρ in {0.2,0.5,0.8}.
Per-task average LLM calls and retry policy as in sampling_plan (affects feasibility but not statistical power).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: Under the stated assumptions (baseline p=0.60, ρ=0.5), N=200 paired tasks yields ~80% power to detect a 10 ppt absolute paired difference. Sensitivity analyses will report MDE across alternative baseline and ρ assumptions.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute MDE for baseline p in {0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7} and ρ in {0.2,0.5,0.8}.
Secondary power checks for stratified analyses (per-task-class N=100 under recommended scenario) reported and interpreted as lower-powered and exploratory.

transformation_families: Verifier JSON feedback → planner constraint application
Emulator execution trace → binary safe/unsafe label extraction
semantic_equivalence_checks: Held-out small reference set (N=40) with gold DSL produced by deterministic generator; require exact parse-equivalence for automated acceptance of transformation.
Round-trip check: DSL → (emulator-simulated validator) → synthesized counterexample → planner-resubmitted DSL should preserve semantics on held-out validation items.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated DSL if deterministic parser reports syntax error or if round-trip parse-normalization changes semantics (non-equivalent AST).
Reject run if emulator returns non-deterministic execution verdict (not reproducible across 2 deterministic replays).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic re-execution of 5% of completed pairs (floor(0.05 × total_confirmatory_items)) chosen by fixed seed for reproducibility; logs and hashes published. No human audit is required or used.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Deterministic parser and serializer with unit tests; mapping validated by exact AST equality on reference corpus; failure logs trigger automatic exclusion of affected items.
residual_risks: Parser/serializer bugs could bias measurement; mitigated by unit tests and automated replays but residual coding error risk remains.
Round-trip semantic-check sample is limited and may not cover all DSL complexities.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Ecological validity: the emulated topologies and synthetic task corpus may not fully represent production network heterogeneity; this is a bounded external-validity limitation.
Possible unknown overlap between public-model pretraining data and synthetic task wording (residual contamination risk not fully eliminable).
Estimator sensitivity to the assumed within-task correlation ρ used in power calculations; reported sensitivity analyses will quantify this.
